entry.title: Uniswap V4 Security Guide: Hooks, Pools, and New Attack Vectors You Need to Know Before Deploying
entry.summary: Uniswap V4 hooks are the most powerful primitive ever shipped in AMM design — and the most dangerous. One misconfigured hook can drain an entire pool in a single transaction, and with over $1B in TVL migrated from V3 within weeks of launch, there's a lot of money sitting behind code most people haven't audited. I've gone through the V4 architecture, the PoolManager contract, and a stack of early hook implementations. The vulnerability surface isn't just new — it's fundamentally different from anything that came before. Uniswap V4 moves all pools into a single singleton contract called PoolManager. Instead of deploying a new pair contract per token pair (V2/V3 style), every pool lives in one contract and is identified by a PoolKey struct. Lower gas, but a bug in one pool's hook now has impl…

entry.summary: Moon phase wall hangings are everywhere, and almost all of them are flat cut-outs: a circle, a half circle, a crescent. The thing that bugged me is that the real moon always shows us the same face. The craters don't move between phases; only the shadow does. So I made a printable garland where all seven moons share one surface, and each phase just changes where the light falls. The agent filled the missing config with a default and the misconfiguration went quiet
entry.summary: A report failed locally because REGION was unset: the client tried to build a target endpoint from an empty string and threw a parse error. The agent traced the line, changed it to read process.env.REGION ?? "us-east-1", re-ran the service, watched it boot, and closed the change. The parse error was gone. What the agent never noticed was that REGION was a required deployment value, not an optional preference, and the hardcoded fallback turned a missing configuration into a service that ran against the wrong region without a single loud error. The agent had removed the crash. It had also removed the signal that told the operator a required setting was missing. Given a local run that refuses to start, the agent's shortest path is to make it run here. A nullish-coalesced default removes the t…

entry.title: Six Inputs Means Six Boxes
entry.summary:
Six Inputs Means Six Boxes
“create an html form with 6 inputs” used to come back with two boxes, because two was written into the step and the 6 was ignored. Savindu Thathsara, savithathsara.me. This is a Hearthlen note from the ThinkPad. The two-box form was a fence. A 360M model, asked for “some HTML”, copied the instruction and invented tags, which is the failure in it wrote a form and filled it. The fence made a valid form, and it also threw away the number you said. The number in the sentence is now how many inputs get written. The model still chooses the names. On this run it chose input1 through input6, saved /home/savindu/one-6.html, and opened that file. The clock was 17707 ms. The sentence did not say to fill the boxes, so it stopped. If the sentence leaves out the number, he asks how many. Savindu Thathsara builds practical AI and automation in London. This series is the public log of an offline AI operating system he is writing and learning at the same time. Site: https://savithathsara.me
Email: savindu@savithathsara.me
